report_meta.supply_chain_link: Lumentum is, alongside Coherent, one of the two big Western VERTICALLY INTEGRATED laser + optics makers — so it spans several tiers of this graph at once. (1) It runs its own indium phosphide (InP) fabs and makes laser CHIPS (EML, CW, pump, narrow-linewidth) — competing with Coherent (see reports/Coherent.json) and consuming InP substrate from suppliers like AXT (see reports/AXT.json) and Sumitomo. (2) It makes optical TRANSCEIVERS (800G/1.6T) — competing with Applied Optoelectronics (see reports/Applied Optoelectronics.json), Coherent, and InnoLight. (3) It makes optical SYSTEMS (OCS switches, WSS, multi-rail). Downstream, it is a direct SUPPLIER TO and PARTNER OF NVIDIA (see reports/NVIDIA.json): NVIDIA invested $2B directly in Lumentum to fund R&D, capacity and U.S. manufacturing for co-packaged optics (CPO). KEY INSIGHT: NVIDIA put $2B into BOTH Lumentum AND Coherent — it is dual-sourcing the InP lasers for its Spectrum-X Photonics CPO switches (the 'laser dies on indium phosphide' NVIDIA cited at GTC 2026). The same InP shortage that benefits AXT upstream is Lumentum's central constraint and pricing lever.

beginner_glossary.Photonics: Technology that uses light (photons) to carry and process information. Lumentum is a photonics company — it makes the lasers and optical parts that move data as light inside and between AI data centers.
beginner_glossary.Indium phosphide (InP): A 'compound semiconductor' crystal — the base material for the high-speed lasers and detectors used in optical networking. InP is scarce and is the key industry bottleneck. Lumentum runs its own InP fabs (and is building more), which is a major advantage.
beginner_glossary.Vertical integration: Doing many supply-chain steps in-house. Lumentum makes the InP wafer, the laser chip, the transceiver, AND the optical system. When lasers are in short supply, owning the laser is a powerful edge over rivals who must buy them.
beginner_glossary.Laser chip: The tiny semiconductor laser at the heart of an optical link. Lumentum's laser chips are a top growth driver; it shipped 2x as many in Q3 FY2026 as a year earlier.
beginner_glossary.EML (Electro-absorption Modulated Laser): A high-speed InP laser used in optical transceivers. EMLs are severely supply-constrained industry-wide; Lumentum says it is ~30%+ short of demand. Higher 'lane speeds' (100-gig, 200-gig) are the leading edge.
beginner_glossary.CW laser (Continuous-Wave): A laser that emits a steady beam; needed in both silicon-photonics transceivers and co-packaged optics. Lumentum sells CW lasers to others AND now uses its own inside its transceivers (in-sourcing for better margin).
beginner_glossary.Pump laser: A laser that 'pumps' (amplifies) optical signals so they can travel long distances. Critical for connecting data centers to each other ('scale-across'). Lumentum says pump lasers are now its MOST supply-constrained product — even tighter than EMLs.
beginner_glossary.Narrow linewidth laser: A very precise laser needed for high-speed (1.6T) and 'coherent' long-distance links. Lumentum's shipments grew 120%+ YoY for nine straight quarters — a high-margin product.
beginner_glossary.Optical transceiver: The plug-in module that converts electricity to light and back so data travels over fiber. Sold by data rate (800G, 1.6T). A core Lumentum 'Systems' product — high revenue but historically LOWER margin than its laser chips.
beginner_glossary.800G / 1.6T / 200G: Speeds. Transceivers are moving from 800G to 1.6T; '200G EML' refers to the per-lane laser speed enabling them. Higher data rates carry higher prices and usually better early-life margins.
beginner_glossary.WSS (wavelength selective switch): An optical 'traffic cop' that routes specific colors (wavelengths) of light without converting them to electricity — used to route huge fiber traffic between data-center buildings.
beginner_glossary.OCS (optical circuit switch): A switch that routes whole light paths directly, saving power in big AI networks (notably Google's TPU clusters). Lumentum has a multi-year, multi-billion-dollar OCS purchase agreement; it uses MEMS (tiny tilting mirrors) technology.
beginner_glossary.CPO (co-packaged optics): Next-gen design that puts the optics right next to the switch/GPU chip to save power, replacing copper in the 'scale-up' network over time. Lumentum calls 'scale-up CPO' its single biggest future growth driver (still 'in its infancy'); its ultra-high-power CW lasers feed it.
beginner_glossary.ELS (external laser source): In a CPO system the laser sits OUTSIDE the chip package in a separate module. Lumentum wants to sell the whole ELS module (not just the bare laser) to capture more dollars per system — its 'vertical integration' play in CPO.
beginner_glossary.Scale-out / scale-up / scale-across: Three layers of AI networking. Scale-out = connecting many systems in a building. Scale-up = connecting chips inside one system (where CPO and copper compete). Scale-across = connecting different data centers to each other (where pump/narrow-linewidth lasers and WSS shine). Lumentum sells into all three.
beginner_glossary.Multi-rail: A new system for moving massive bandwidth BETWEEN AI data centers; uses many pump lasers, so it increases Lumentum's content. An emerging 'scale-across' opportunity.
beginner_glossary.Components vs Systems: Lumentum's two reporting segments. Components = laser chips and optical components (higher margin); Systems = transceivers, OCS, WSS, industrial lasers (bigger revenue, transceivers lower margin).
beginner_glossary.MEMS: Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems — here, tiny movable mirrors used in Lumentum's OCS switches. Its claimed technology edge over emerging competitors.
beginner_glossary.3D sensing: Lasers (VCSELs) used in consumer devices (e.g., phone face-unlock). A legacy Lumentum business, now small relative to AI datacom.
beginner_glossary.Supply-demand imbalance: How far orders exceed what Lumentum can ship. It cites >30% on EMLs and even higher on pump lasers — i.e., it is 'sold out' and undershipping demand, which supports pricing.
beginner_glossary.LTA (long-term agreement): A multi-year supply contract. Lumentum's can include customer prepayments, 'take-or-pay' commitments, and price increases — customer 'skin in the game' that helps fund Lumentum's capacity expansion. NVIDIA's $2B investment is the marquee example.
beginner_glossary.GAAP vs non-GAAP: GAAP = official accounting (everything included). Non-GAAP = adjusted (strips out items like stock-based comp and amortization). Lumentum reports mostly non-GAAP on calls; the gap is large, so always check GAAP too.
beginner_glossary.Convertible notes / diluted shares: Lumentum has bonds that can convert into stock. So its DILUTED share count (~95–102M) is well above its basic shares outstanding (~78M). This matters for valuation: the 'true' fully-diluted market value is meaningfully higher than the headline market cap.
beginner_glossary.Gross / operating margin: Gross margin = revenue minus direct product cost; operating margin = after all operating costs. Lumentum's non-GAAP gross margin jumped to 47.9% and operating margin to 32.2% in Q3 FY2026 — both rising fast.
beginner_glossary.P/E and P/S: P/E = price ÷ earnings per share; P/S = market value ÷ revenue. Lumentum's GAAP P/E (~175x) is distorted by its still-small GAAP earnings; analysts lean on non-GAAP earnings and on P/S — which is very high here (~29x on basic shares, higher fully diluted).

company_snapshot.what_it_is: Lumentum is a vertically integrated photonics company. It runs its own indium phosphide (InP) fabs, makes the laser chips (EML, CW, pump, narrow-linewidth) and optical components, builds optical transceivers (800G/1.6T), and makes optical systems (OCS switches, WSS). Its products are foundational to AI data-center networking. It also has smaller legacy industrial-laser and 3D-sensing businesses.
company_snapshot.ceo: Michael Hurlston (President & CEO); Wajid Ali (EVP & CFO); Wupen Yuen (President, Global Business Units)
company_snapshot.founded: Spun off from JDS Uniphase (JDSU) in 2015. Fiscal year ends in late June.
company_snapshot.where_it_sits_in_the_chain: Spans multiple tiers: component (InP laser chips, pump/narrow-linewidth lasers) → switch_system (transceivers, OCS, WSS, multi-rail). Consumes InP substrate (AXT/Sumitomo) upstream; sells to hyperscalers, systems makers, and NVIDIA (which is also a $2B investor).
company_snapshot.manufacturing_note: Owns the full optical stack. Laser-chip wafer fab in Japan is 'fully allocated'; pump-laser capacity ramping at its Rose Orchard (California) site; in March 2026 it announced a FIFTH InP fab in Greensboro, North Carolina (converting from gallium arsenide to InP), online ~2028, plus expanded transceiver assembly in Thailand. Heavy emphasis on U.S. manufacturing.
products: Laser chips: EML (100G/200G lane), CW lasers, ultra-high-power CW lasers for CPO — the highest-margin growth engine
Scale-across components: pump lasers, narrow-linewidth laser assemblies, wavelength selective switches (WSS) — supply-constrained, high-margin
Optical transceivers (800G, 1.6T) — large revenue ('Systems'), historically lower margin, improving
Optical Circuit Switches (OCS) — multi-year, multi-billion-dollar agreement; MEMS-based
Emerging: co-packaged optics (CPO) lasers + ELS modules; multi-rail systems; data-center thermal/other adjacencies
Legacy: industrial lasers, cable-access, 3D-sensing (VCSELs) — now small relative to AI datacom

business_model.summary: Lumentum makes money selling photonic components and systems, now overwhelmingly driven by AI data-center demand. The thesis: AI networks need enormous numbers of lasers and optical systems; the key input (InP lasers) is in severe shortage; and Lumentum is one of very few players that makes its OWN InP and lasers — so it captures more value, can raise prices, and is shielded from shortages. The richest margins come from its 'Components' (laser chips, pump/narrow-linewidth lasers); 'Systems' (transceivers, OCS) add big revenue and are improving in margin.
how_they_make_money: Components ($533M, 66% of Q3 FY2026 revenue): laser chips (EML/CW), pump lasers, narrow-linewidth laser assemblies, WSS. Grew +20% QoQ / +77% YoY; the main margin driver. These are 'effectively sold out.'
Systems ($275M, 34% of revenue): cloud transceivers (800G/1.6T), OCS, industrial lasers, cable access. Grew +24% QoQ / +121% YoY, led by cloud transceivers (+40% sequentially).
In-sourcing for margin: Lumentum now puts its OWN CW lasers into ~20% of its transceiver modules (rising over time), capturing more value per unit.
Long-term agreements (LTAs): multi-year deals (prepayment / take-or-pay / price increases) that fund capacity — NVIDIA's $2B direct investment is the flagship.
competitive_moat_analyst_view: Vertical integration: owns InP fabs + laser chips + transceivers + systems. In an InP-short market, controlling the scarce laser is a durable edge over assemblers. [Q3 FY2026 call]

Scarce, high-margin components: pump lasers and narrow-linewidth lasers (for 'scale-across') are even more constrained than EMLs and carry rich margins — a less-appreciated profit lever. [Q3 FY2026 call]
OCS leadership: a multi-year, multi-billion-dollar OCS agreement and MEMS technology that management believes rivals can't match near-term. [Q3 FY2026 call]
NVIDIA partnership: a $2B direct investment plus CPO supply, validating Lumentum's ultra-high-power laser roadmap and funding U.S. capacity. [Q3 FY2026 call]
Pricing power: a >30% supply-demand gap lets Lumentum raise prices and sign favorable LTAs. [Q3 FY2026 call]

segments.what_it_is: Laser chips (EML, CW) plus 'scale-across' components: pump lasers, narrow-linewidth laser assemblies, and WSS. The high-margin engine.
segments.notes: Record EML shipments (100G lane; 200G EML revenue more than doubled QoQ); narrow-linewidth +120% YoY (9th straight quarter of growth); pump lasers +80% YoY. 'Effectively sold out.' Ultra-high-power CW lasers for CPO ramping on plan.

revenue_streams.analyst_view: This is now an AI-optics story with two engines. Components (~66%) is the profit driver — laser chips and the under-appreciated 'scale-across' lasers (pumps, narrow-linewidth) that are even scarcer than EMLs. Systems (~34%) brings big revenue growth (transceivers, OCS) at lower-but-improving margins. The whole business is supply-constrained, so near-term revenue is gated by how fast Lumentum can add capacity, not by demand. The biggest future swing factor — scale-up CPO — is barely in the numbers yet.

industry_trends.trend: AI data centers drive an optical-laser boom
industry_trends.why_it_matters: Every AI cluster needs vast optical networking; Lumentum makes the scarce lasers at its core.
industry_trends.evidence: Revenue +90% YoY; demand exceeds supply by >30% on EMLs; LTAs and a $2B NVIDIA investment underwrite capacity. [Q3 FY2026 call, 2026-05-05]

industry_trends.why_it_matters: InP lasers (EML, CW, pump) are the binding constraint industry-wide; whoever can make more, faster, wins share and pricing.

competitors.landscape_summary: Lumentum and Coherent are the two large Western vertically integrated laser + optics makers, competing across laser chips, transceivers, OCS, and CPO. In transceivers, Chinese players InnoLight and Eoptolink lead on volume, and Applied Optoelectronics also competes. In DSP/switch silicon and CPO, Broadcom and Marvell intersect. Lumentum's distinctive strength is its laser-chip portfolio (EML/CW/pump/narrow-linewidth) and OCS.

key_competitors.note: The closest peer — also vertically integrated (InP + lasers + transceivers + OCS/CPO) and also took a $2B NVIDIA investment. Direct rival across nearly every product line (see reports/Coherent.json).
U.S. transceiver maker with in-house lasers; smaller, also riding the AI/InP wave (see reports/Applied Optoelectronics.json).
China; the volume leader in 800G/1.6T AI transceivers — competes hard on scale/price.
Optical DSP and custom silicon; goes inside transceivers — partner and competitor by layer.
Switch silicon and a CPO developer; competitor in co-packaged optics/networking.
Coherent/DCI systems and ZR optics — competes in 'scale-across'/transport.
Upstream suppliers of InP wafers. Lumentum runs its own InP fabs too, so it is partly a vertically integrated peer; the shared InP shortage affects all.

market_share_facts: Lumentum and Coherent are the dominant Western laser-chip + transceiver suppliers; Chinese makers (InnoLight, Eoptolink) lead transceiver volumes. [industry context]
Lumentum holds a leading position in OCS (multi-year, multi-billion-dollar agreement) and in scale-across lasers (pumps, narrow-linewidth). [Q3 FY2026 call, 2026-05-05]
competitors.supply_chain_cross_reference: Lumentum's peer Coherent, transceiver rival AAOI, substrate supplier AXT, and DSP/switch players Marvell/Broadcom are all nodes in this repo. Its customer-and-investor NVIDIA is at reports/NVIDIA.json. Notably NVIDIA invested $2B in BOTH Lumentum and Coherent — dual-sourcing CPO lasers.
competitors.differentiation_analyst_view: Lumentum's edge is its laser-chip depth (EML/CW/pump/narrow-linewidth) plus OCS — owning scarce inputs in a shortage. Its relative weakness versus Coherent has been transceiver margins (historically below peers), which it is now improving via in-sourced CW lasers, better yields, and contract manufacturing. Main risks: Chinese transceiver competition, a future easing of the laser shortage (oversupply), and execution on three simultaneous big ramps (pumps, OCS, CPO lasers).

financial_performance.analyst_view: The inflection is dramatic: revenue +90% YoY, non-GAAP operating margin up >2,100 bps YoY, and a fortress balance sheet ($3.17B cash) after NVIDIA's $2B. Two things to hold: (1) GAAP earnings, while now positive, are far smaller than the share price implies (hence a ~175x GAAP P/E), so read the operating story in non-GAAP terms; and (2) the share count is rising (convertibles + dilution), and the biggest growth driver (scale-up CPO) is barely started — so the valuation leans heavily on future ramps executing.

valuation.analyst_view: Lumentum offers a genuine, well-documented inflection — scarce lasers, surging margins, OCS leadership, and a $2B NVIDIA partnership. But valuation is the catch and is even more demanding than peer Coherent (~29–35x sales vs ~11x), partly because convertibles inflate the diluted share count. The extreme 52-week range is the clearest signal of how expectation- and headline-driven this stock is; almost everything has to go right to justify the price.

Three huge simultaneous ramps (pump lasers, OCS, CPO lasers) are all gated by capacity; management calls OCS 'the biggest single tightrope.' Slips directly cap revenue.
Today's pricing power depends on the >30% supply gap. Competitors are all adding capacity; if the shortage eases, pricing and margins could reverse.
InnoLight and Eoptolink lead transceiver volumes and compete on price/scale, pressuring Lumentum's lower-margin Systems business.
Lumentum's transceiver margins trail peers; the bull case assumes they keep improving via in-sourced lasers, yields, and contract manufacturing.
Diluted share count (~95–102M) is well above basic (~78M) and rising; this inflates the true market value and means per-share growth lags revenue growth.
A $2B NVIDIA stake and a few large hyperscaler/OCS customers concentrate demand; OCS in particular leans on one or two buyers.
Demand tracks hyperscaler AI spending; a capex slowdown would hit a very high-multiple, optics-levered name hard.
The largest future driver (scale-up CPO) is 'in its infancy' and the Greensboro fab is ~2028 — much of the thesis is years out and uncertain.
Headline numbers on calls are non-GAAP; GAAP earnings are much smaller, so reliance on adjustments requires scrutiny.

final_research_summary.one_paragraph: Lumentum Holdings (LITE) is a vertically integrated photonics company and, alongside Coherent, one of the two big Western makers of the lasers and optical systems that AI data centers run on. It owns indium phosphide (InP) fabs and makes laser chips (EML, CW, pump, narrow-linewidth), optical transceivers (800G/1.6T), and optical systems (OCS switches, WSS) — so it both competes with substrate maker AXT and transceiver makers Coherent/AAOI, and supplies (and is partly owned by) NVIDIA. The fundamentals just inflected dramatically: Q3 FY2026 (reported 2026-05-05) revenue hit a record $808.4M (+90% YoY), with Components +77% YoY and Systems +121% YoY, non-GAAP gross margin jumping to 47.9% (+1,270 bps YoY) and non-GAAP operating margin to 32.2% (+2,140 bps YoY); GAAP EPS was $1.50, non-GAAP EPS $2.37. The balance sheet holds $3.17B of cash after NVIDIA's $2B direct investment (which funds R&D, capacity, and U.S. manufacturing, including a new fifth InP fab in Greensboro, NC, online ~2028). Demand exceeds supply by >30% on EMLs and even more on pump lasers, so Lumentum is 'sold out,' raising prices and signing customer-funded LTAs; management guided Q4 to a record ~$985M and reaffirmed a long-term $2B/quarter revenue goal as transceivers, OCS, scale-out CPO, scale-up CPO, and scale-across all layer in. The catch is valuation: at ~$922 the stock trades around 29x trailing sales on basic shares — and closer to ~35x on the fully-diluted share count (convertible notes push diluted shares to ~95–102M vs ~78M basic) — with a 52-week range of $82 to $1,086 (an ~13x swing). The facts (record revenue, margin surge, laser shortage, OCS lead, NVIDIA deal, fortress balance sheet) are real and well-documented; what is PRICED is years of sustained shortage-driven growth, margin expansion toward targets, and big new ramps (OCS and especially scale-up CPO, which is 'in its infancy') executing on time against Chinese competition. The core debate is valuation + execution + how long the laser shortage lasts — not whether demand exists.

what_is_assumption_or_opinion: ASSUMPTION: The laser/InP shortage persists long enough to keep pricing power, even as all competitors add capacity.
ASSUMPTION: The three big ramps (pumps, OCS, scale-up CPO) execute roughly on plan and scale-up CPO becomes material from 2027.
OPINION: Read the business in non-GAAP terms — GAAP earnings are small, making the ~175x GAAP P/E misleading.
OPINION: At ~29–35x sales (note the convertible-driven dilution), Lumentum is even more demanding than peer Coherent; downside is large if the shortage eases or ramps slip.
